common_name: Louis XIV Rose (Velvety Dark Crimson China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Louis XIV is an 1859 French China rose prized for unusually dark, velvety crimson color rare among roses of its era.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants 2-3 feet apart for its compact, bushy habit. Louis XIV bears richly fragrant, velvety dark crimson-maroon blooms that appear almost black in bud, held on a low, twiggy bush with dark reddish new growth, flowering in repeated flushes from spring through frost. It performs best with light pruning in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood, since heavy cutting sacrifices the small flowering twigs that carry most of its bloom.

common_name: James Sprunt Rose (Climbing Crimson China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall against a support; James Sprunt is a mid-19th-century American climbing sport of the China rose 'Cramoisi Superieur,' retaining its parent's crimson color on a much more vigorous, climbing cane habit.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil near a fence, trellis, or pillar, spacing plants 4-6 feet apart to allow room for long canes. James Sprunt produces clusters of double, rich crimson blooms with a light fragrance in continuous flushes from spring through frost, on long, arching canes that need tying in to a support as they grow. Prune after the main flush to remove old or crowded wood and train new canes horizontally to encourage more lateral flowering shoots.

common_name: Serratipetala Rose (Fringed-Petal China Rose, Oeillet Parfait)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Serratipetala, also sold as Oeillet Parfait, is an antique China rose distinguished by petals with jagged, fringed edges unlike any other China variety.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants 2.5-3.5 feet apart. Serratipetala bears small, double, carmine-pink flowers whose petals are distinctively cut and fringed along the edges, giving blooms a ragged, carnation-like look, and it flowers in repeated flushes from spring through frost. Like other China roses it tolerates heat and humidity well with minimal spray input. Prune lightly in late winter to shape the bush and remove dead or weak wood.

common_name: Madame Eugene Resal Rose (Coppery Bicolor China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Madame Eugene Resal is an 1890s French China rose grown for its unusual coppery-orange and carmine-pink bicolor blooms.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants 2-3 feet apart for its compact habit. Madame Eugene Resal bears semi-double blooms in a striking bicolor of coppery-orange outer petals against carmine-pink inner petals, a color combination unusual among antique roses, flowering in repeated flushes from spring through frost. The bush stays low and bushy, suiting borders and containers. Prune lightly in late winter to remove dead wood and maintain its compact form.

common_name: Eugene de Beauharnais Rose (Purple-Crimson Antique China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Eugene de Beauharnais is an 1830s French antique China rose noted for growing considerably larger than most Chinas, with deep purple-crimson color.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants 3-4 feet apart to accommodate its unusually vigorous growth for a China rose. Eugene de Beauharnais bears semi-double to double blooms in deep amaranth-purple to crimson tones, flowering in repeated flushes from spring through frost on a bush notably larger and more vigorous than most members of its class. Prune lightly in late winter to control size and remove crossing or weak wood.

common_name: Beauty of Rosemawr Rose (Soft Pink Tea-China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Beauty of Rosemawr is an early 20th-century American Tea-China rose valued for its soft pink color and repeat bloom.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants 2-3 feet apart. Beauty of Rosemawr bears double, soft pink blooms with a light, pleasant fragrance on a bushy, free-flowering plant that repeats reliably from spring through frost. Its combination of Tea and China heritage gives it good heat tolerance alongside refined, soft-colored flowers. Prune lightly in late winter to remove dead wood and keep the plant tidy.
